editorial_reason: A totally ordered field has the ordinary field operations and inverses with a compatible total order. The previously screened commutative-unital field supplies this prerequisite; no least-upper-bound property is inferred from the field axioms.

The supremum property quantifies over arbitrary nonempty upper-bounded subsets A of S; the non-strict subset relation supplies that underlying set inclusion without demanding properness or a total order.
The real-number axiomatic structure is first a totally ordered field: totality, translation invariance, and positive-scalar multiplication compatibility precede the extra supremum axiom.

Dedekind completeness means every nonempty bounded-above subset has a least upper bound in R. This is an additional order-theoretic condition on the ordered field, not a consequence of field axioms alone.

The piecewise absolute-value function uses the total order and additive inverses of the real-number system. The newly screened complete ordered real field supplies this exact ambient object without reversing the dependence through epsilon-delta limits.
